source_anchor: Final-order PDF front matter identifies Order No. PSC-2026-0022-S-EI in Docket No. 20250011-EI.
what_it_says: FPL recovery proof now has a commission-order anchor, not only company-slide proxy evidence.
what_it_does_not_say: It does not allocate every project or capital category to a revenue requirement.

source_anchor: Final order describes a rate plan beginning January 1, 2026 and continuing until the later of December 31, 2029 or new base rates.
what_it_says: FPL has a bounded approved recovery term for base-rate framework analysis.
what_it_does_not_say: It does not prove individual project returns.

source_anchor: Final order states that rates and cost-recovery clause proceedings during the term use a 10.95 percent ROE.
what_it_says: The FPL bridge moves from regulated-return proxy to approved allowed-return evidence.
what_it_does_not_say: It is not equity return realized by investors or project-level IRR.

source_anchor: Final order and settlement terms describe an authorized ROE range around the 10.95 percent midpoint.
what_it_says: There is an official corridor for allowed return analysis.
what_it_does_not_say: It does not show actual earned ROE or project-level return.

source_anchor: Final order/settlement terms identify a 59.6 percent equity ratio based on investor sources.
what_it_says: FPL recovery proof now has an official capital-structure input.
what_it_does_not_say: It is not a project-specific funding-source allocation.

source_anchor: SEC settlement exhibit states FPL is authorized to increase base rates and service charges by an amount intended to generate additional annual revenue of 945 million dollars in 2026.
what_it_says: The settlement amount is lower than the as-filed request and gives an approved-framework revenue denominator.
what_it_does_not_say: It is not a project-by-project revenue requirement.

source_anchor: SEC settlement exhibit states the 2027 increase is intended to generate an additional 705 million dollars over then-current base rates.
what_it_says: FPL has an official 2027 base-rate step for the recovery bridge.
what_it_does_not_say: It does not isolate the share tied to AI/data-center load, solar, battery, or transmission.

metric_label: Solar and Battery Base Rate Adjustment project years
source_anchor: SEC settlement exhibit authorizes FPL to petition for base-rate recovery for solar projects entering service in 2027-2029 and battery storage projects entering service in 2028-2029.
what_it_says: Solar and battery recovery mechanics are visible as a named mechanism.
what_it_does_not_say: It does not prove approval for each future SoBRA project before petition/review.

source_anchor: SEC settlement exhibit identifies 1.155 billion dollars of deferred tax liabilities in the Rate Stabilization Mechanism amount.
what_it_says: FPL settlement includes a cash/rate-stability mechanism that can affect customer bill/revenue timing.
what_it_does_not_say: It is not operating output or project-return proof.

source_anchor: SPPCRC filing testimony says total jurisdictional revenue requirements including true-up amounts are 859.244393 million dollars for January-December 2026.
what_it_says: FPL has program-level cost-recovery revenue-requirement evidence for storm-protection investment.
what_it_does_not_say: It is not proof for non-storm projects or all grid capital.

metric_label: SPP program projected revenue requirements before true-up
source_anchor: SPPCRC testimony separates 873.977263 million dollars of projected program revenue requirements before true-up effects.
what_it_says: Storm-protection program recovery can be parsed into a schedule-level bridge.
what_it_does_not_say: It does not establish project-level ROE or full capital-use attribution.

source_anchor: PSC staff recommendation summarizes FPL's as-filed request as about 1.55 billion dollars of additional gross annual revenue for 2026.
what_it_says: The extraction now preserves request-versus-settlement delta context.
what_it_does_not_say: It is not approved final recovery.

source_anchor: PSC staff recommendation summarizes the as-filed 2027 request as 927 million dollars of additional gross annual revenue.
what_it_says: The table can compare requested and settlement revenue increases.
what_it_does_not_say: It is not approved final recovery.

source_anchor: PSC staff recommendation states FPL asserted a requested ROE midpoint of 11.90 percent.
what_it_says: The final-order/settlement 10.95 percent ROE can be compared with the request baseline.
what_it_does_not_say: It is not the approved settlement ROE.

metric_label: new renewables and storage origination added to backlog
source_anchor: NextEra Q1 2026 SEC exhibit reports record new renewables and storage origination, adding 4 GW to backlog.
what_it_says: Energy Resources backlog growth is now visible in an SEC exhibit.
what_it_does_not_say: It does not disclose project customer price or return.

metric_label: battery storage origination within backlog additions
source_anchor: NextEra Q1 2026 SEC exhibit identifies 1.3 GW of battery storage origination within the quarter's backlog additions.
what_it_says: The technology split improves contracted-output quality.
what_it_does_not_say: It does not prove battery project economics or financing.

metric_label: new cost-effective solar placed in service
source_anchor: NextEra Q1 2026 SEC exhibit says FPL placed approximately 600 MW of new cost-effective solar into service.
what_it_says: FPL has in-service output evidence that can be reconciled with recovery mechanisms.
what_it_does_not_say: It does not prove the revenue requirement for each solar project.

metric_label: FPL owned and operated solar portfolio
source_anchor: NextEra Q1 2026 SEC exhibit says the new solar additions put FPL's owned and operated solar portfolio above 8.5 GW.
what_it_says: The operating asset base is visible as a denominator for recovery analysis.
what_it_does_not_say: It is not a project-return calculation.

source_anchor: NextEra IR release states Energy Resources and Meta reached approximately 2.5 GW of clean-energy contracts.
what_it_says: A named hyperscaler customer route upgrades backlog quality beyond anonymous aggregate backlog.
what_it_does_not_say: It does not disclose PPA price, margin, debt financing, or project IRR.

source_anchor: NextEra IR release ties the 2.5 GW milestone to 11 power purchase agreements and two energy storage agreements.
what_it_says: The customer-contract row has agreement-count evidence.
what_it_does_not_say: It does not disclose contract tenors or pricing.

metric_label: Meta solar project PPAs across ERCOT/SPP/MISO
source_anchor: NextEra IR release says Meta PPAs enable 2.1 GW of clean energy through nine solar projects across ERCOT, SPP, and MISO.
what_it_says: The release links named customer, markets, technology, and project count.
what_it_does_not_say: It does not identify each project's capex or return.

metric_label: PNM Rate 36B solar and storage support
source_anchor: NextEra IR release says four New Mexico projects provide 190 MW solar and 168 MW battery storage to support PNM's system through Rate 36B.
what_it_says: The row links customer demand to a named utility rate mechanism.
what_it_does_not_say: It does not disclose the underlying PNM tariff economics or project financing.

metric_label: Meta project online window and jobs
source_anchor: NextEra IR release says the 2.5 GW across 13 projects is scheduled online between 2026 and 2028 and could create up to 2,440 construction jobs.
what_it_says: The release gives in-service timing for named-customer contracted capacity.
what_it_does_not_say: It does not provide project cost or return.

metric_label: Energy Resources net generating capacity in operation
source_anchor: NextEra IR release says Energy Resources had approximately 33,410 MW of net generating capacity in operation at year-end 2024.
what_it_says: The operating platform denominator is visible for backlog-to-base comparison.
what_it_does_not_say: It does not prove economics for the Meta contracts.
